subject: NIMBLE doesn't compile nested nimbleFunctions with default NA arguments

messages.author: 51531762f4fb63a1
messages.subject: NIMBLE doesn't compile nested nimbleFunctions with default NA arguments
parts:
Hi all,

Sorry, I accidentally posted this without finishing it earlier!

I have a problem in that I can't get nested nimbleFunctions to compile when using NAs as default values.
As a reprex, I've used the custom distribution example from the NIMBLE manual below.

The pmyexp function takes an optional truncation argument (zU below) which by default is a missing value.
This compiles fine. However, if I then call this function within another nimbleFunction (rmyexp below)
it won't compile. I think I've narrowed it down to the fact that the pmyexp(zU, rate) doesn't explicitly set zU, but I have
no idea how to do this. It should reduce to the default I think. I've tried various things, including setting dummy
variables within rmyexp, but cannot seem to get this to work.

Any pointers greatly appreciated.

Many thanks,

TJ

library(nimble)

## set up dummy CDF
pmyexp <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(q = double(0), rate = double(0, default = 1),
                 zU = double(0, default = as.numeric(NA)),
                 lower.tail = integer(0, default = 1),
                 log.p = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    if(!is.na(zU)) {
      ldenom <- log(1.0 - exp(-rate * zU))
    } else {
      ldenom <- 0
    }
    if(!lower.tail) {
      logp <- -rate * q - ldenom
      if(log.p) return(logp) else return(exp(logp))
    } else {
      p <- log(1 - exp(-rate * q)) - ldenom
      if(!log.p) return(exp(p))
      else return(p)
    }
  })

## set up dummy random sampler
rmyexp <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n = integer(0), rate = double(0, default = 1),
                 zU = double(0, default = as.numeric(NA))) {
    returnType(double(0))
    if(n != 1) print("rmyexp only allows n = 1; using n = 1.")
    dev <- runif(1, 0, 1)
    if(!is.na(zU)) {
        dev <- dev * pmyexp(zU, rate)
    }
    return(-log(1-dev) / rate)
})

## compiles fine
compileNimble(pmyexp)

## try to compile and throws an error
## (should use default zU = NA in pmyexp call below)
compileNimble(rmyexp)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: NIMBLE doesn't compile nested nimbleFunctions with default NA arguments
parts:
Hi TJ,

Thanks for the inquiry and use case.

As it happens, there was just another issue revolving around support for NA through compilation.  My response to that (a few minutes ago) may also be relevant to your need.

What it comes down to at the moment is that using a default value of NA is not going to work through compilation.  A couple of options would be to use NaN instead, to choose a protocol like -1 to indicate "NA", or to use an additional argument that is a logical to take the role of the is.na(zU).

Incidentally, I don't totally follow that you have a zU in pmyexp and a zU in rmyexp that is passed as the q argument to pmyexp.  You probably have the logic worked out but that seemed potentially confusing in trying to read your code.

HTH.

-Perry

messages.author: 51531762f4fb63a1
messages.subject: Re: NIMBLE doesn't compile nested nimbleFunctions with default NA arguments
parts:
Hi Perry,

Thanks very much for the swift reply. I will also take a look at your other post.

Weirdly it seems to work fine to have NA as a default when compiling, as long as you don't have nested nimbleFunctions. I did think about using negative values instead of NAs, but NAs are a touch neater.

You are correct that there is method to the madness about passing zU to rmyexp and then ignoring it in the nested call to pmyexp. It makes more sense it the actual code, but that's more convoluted to post! That being said, I am beginning to think there might be a better way to do it in any case.

Thanks very much for your input, and thanks for developing Nimble, it's a great piece of software!

Cheers,

TJ

Thanks TJ.

You're right: The NA default does work when called from R, but not when the compiler generates code for a call from another compiled function that needs to rely on the default.

Glad you can work around it.
